articles.label: Gift Guide
articles.title: The Best Christmas Gifts for Dad
articles.intro: From the dad who says he wants nothing to the one who already owns every tool. Here's what to get him this year.

image.alt: Wrapped red and white Christmas presents

body: Ask a dad what he wants for Christmas and you'll hear the same thing every year: nothing. He means it, too. If he needed it, he'd have bought it in October.

So skip the things he needs and look for the things he'd enjoy but would never buy for himself. A better way to make his morning coffee. A proper glass for the drink he pours on Friday night. A game that gets the whole family around the table.
Everything below has been picked with that in mind. None of it is a novelty he'll forget by New Year.

articles.label: Ideas
articles.title: Unique Gifts for Someone Who Has Everything
articles.intro: When the usual ideas are taken, go for something they'd never think to buy themselves.

image.alt: Rows of vinyl records in a record shop

body: Some people are impossible to shop for. They own the gadgets, they've read the books, and anything they wanted they bought themselves last week.
The trick is to stop looking for something they need. Look for something they'd never think of instead: a small pleasure, an odd find or a nicer version of an everyday thing.
These are the gifts we reach for when the usual ideas are already taken.

articles.label: Tested & Loved
articles.title: Clever Gadgets That Make Everyday Life Easier

image.alt: A tidy desk with laptop, coffee and notebook

body: A good gadget earns its place. It solves a small problem you'd stopped noticing, and a month later you can't remember how you managed without it.
We skipped anything that needs an app to turn on, anything that will end up in a drawer, and anything that only looks clever in an advert.
What's left is a short list of things that get used every day.

articles.label: Essay
articles.title: Thoughtful Gifts That Don't Feel Ordinary
articles.intro: A few ideas for giving with a bit more meaning.

image.alt: A hand writing in a journal beside a coffee cup

body: A thoughtful gift doesn't have to be expensive. It has to show that you were paying attention.
Think about how they spend a quiet evening, what they keep on their desk, or the small thing they keep saying they'll get round to buying. That's usually where the good ideas are.
Here are a few gifts that feel personal without needing a monogram.

articles.label: Gift Guide
articles.title: The Best Gifts for Dad, Any Time of Year
articles.intro: Birthday, Father's Day or just because. Gifts he'll use long after the wrapping paper is gone.

image.alt: A drink being poured over a large ice cube in a glass

body: Dads are hard to buy for because they rarely ask for anything. The good news is that most of them have a few simple pleasures, and a gift that makes one of those better nearly always lands.
Start with what he already does. If he makes coffee every morning, upgrade the coffee. If he's the one who plans the camping trip, get him something for the trip.
These are our favourite picks for dads right now.

articles.label: On a budget
articles.title: Great Gifts Under $25
articles.intro: Small gifts that don't feel small. Good for stockings, Secret Santa and thank-yous.

image.alt: A frosted cupcake on a bright yellow background

body: A small budget is not a problem. Some of the best gifts cost less than a takeaway.
At this price, go for one nice thing rather than a bundle of cheap ones. A well-made mug or a good notebook beats a novelty set every time.
Everything here costs less than $25.

articles.label: On a budget
articles.title: Great Gifts Under $50
articles.intro: Enough to get something that feels special, without overthinking it.

image.alt: Two lit candles in amber glass jars

body: Fifty dollars is a comfortable budget for most occasions. It's enough for something that lasts, but not so much that it feels like a statement.
Look for gifts that turn an everyday habit into a small treat: a better cup of coffee, a calmer evening or a more fun game night.
Everything here costs less than $50.

articles.label: Gift Guide
articles.title: Gifts for Tech Lovers
articles.intro: For the person who reads reviews for fun and already owns the obvious stuff.

image.alt: Vintage computers and keyboards lit in pink and blue

body: Buying tech for someone who loves tech is risky. They know more than you do, and they've probably already picked the exact model they want.
So don't try to guess the big purchase. Go for the things around it: a nicer desk setup, something with a bit of retro charm, or an accessory they wouldn't buy for themselves.
These are safe bets for people who love their gadgets.
